verdict.rationale: The DGX B200 is inherently a physical, on-premises AI system sold to enterprises for deployment in their own data centers — documentation covers self-hosted operations including node health monitoring, cluster/data-center-level GPU administration, power redundancy, BMC/Redfish/IPMI/SNMP/KVM remote management, and container tooling (Docker/NVIDIA Container Toolkit) for running workloads locally. Community evidence corroborates real-world self-hosted/on-prem use and virtualization setups (NVLink partitioning, VFIO passthrough) for isolating GPUs in self-managed infrastructure. Missing for 10: no independent audit of ease of full self-hosting at scale beyond DGX SuperPOD marketing, and no evidence of an open, non-NVIDIA software stack for self-hosting outside the vendor ecosystem.
